name: Ultrasound skin tightening (microfocused)
lead: Ultrasound skin tightening uses intense focused ultrasound (IFUS), also called microfocused ultrasound, to deliver heat at specific depths beneath the skin while sparing the surface, with the aim of tightening and lifting sagging tissue without surgery.[1][2] Branded systems such as Ulthera are used in registered trials on the face, neck and arms.[3]

Published clinical studies include a rater-blinded prospective cohort study of the face and neck with brow lift as the main target, a single-treatment study in 22 Korean patients with blinded clinician assessment, a multiple-pass study of the lower face and neck, and a study of infraorbital laxity.[4][5][1][6] The introductions of these papers describe the technique as having excellent safety but limited efficacy in the case of nonablative tightening generally.[4]
A 2025 paper examined a high-intensity parallel ultrasound variant.[7]
infobox: Face, neck, infraorbital area, upper arms, elbows
Described as minimal in the studies

paras: IFUS produces thermal effects at different depths while sparing the overlying epidermis.[2] High-intensity focused ultrasound in general heats tissue at a focal point; Wikipedia notes tissue heated above 60 degrees Celsius for more than a second is irreversibly damaged.[8]

A rater-blinded prospective cohort at a dermatology clinic assessed brow-lift efficacy in the context of full face and neck treatment.[4] A study of 22 Korean patients assessed outcomes after a single IFUS session with blinded clinicians and pathology.[2] A study of multiple-pass treatment evaluated lower face and neck laxity,[1] and another assessed infraorbital laxity as a non-surgical alternative to blepharoplasty.[6] The abstracts available here do not give detailed effect sizes.

Registered trials include combinations with thread lifting and with neck liposuction (the latter withdrawn), and studies of the neck, elbows, upper arms and face using the Ulthera system, plus an ongoing 273-participant trial of a high-intensity device for submental and neck laxity.[9][10][11][12]

card.summary: Heat from focused ultrasound aimed beneath the skin to tighten the face and neck; published cohort studies exist but detailed effect sizes were not verified.

quick.overview:
Microfocused ultrasound treatments send focused ultrasound energy under the skin to heat deeper layers and tighten sagging areas such as the brow, jawline and neck.

Published cohort studies report on facial and neck laxity, and several trials are registered.
quick.mechanism: Focused ultrasound heats tissue at set depths below the surface while sparing the epidermis.
quick.risks: Studies describe the safety profile of nonablative tightening as good with limited efficacy in general; detailed adverse events were not in the abstracts available.
